items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Miller was in Europe, playing with Alex Welch, and I had just finished the 28 straight days with the Jazz of the Swing Era and they went back to the states and Eddie Lockjaw Davis, Ben Webster, Eddie Miller and I went on this thing called Just for Tenor

ctx.x: Now, again, I don't mean to say that I didn't admire Hawkins, which I did, and I thought really that Ben Webster was the best ballad tenor player I had ever heard of.

Now, there are many tenor players I admire. I admire Stan Getz, there are so many different players that I have tremendous regard for. Eddie Miller who played in beautiful taste, lovely sound and all that.

But I think that Lester Young had the thing that no one else had, and he was not frightened to come out and play that little tiny sound when everybody else was blowing his brains out. And Lester also had -- he had a marvelous sense of the ridiculous, not in his music, but in his way of life. I will never forget.
